quests.passage: A regional airline found that flights operated with its newest aircraft model had higher on-time departure rates than flights using older aircraft models. Both aircraft types were flown on similar routes, by similarly experienced pilot crews, and departed from the same gates at the same airports, according to the airline's fleet assignment records.
logicChain: Similar routes, similar crew experience, same gates for both aircraft types -> newer aircraft: higher on-time rates -> common competing factors ruled out, leaving aircraft model itself as the more plausible remaining explanation
logicChainSteps: Similar routes, similar crew experience, same gates for both aircraft types
newer aircraft: higher on-time rates
common competing factors ruled out, leaving aircraft model itself as the more plausible remaining explanation
quests.conclusion: Since routes, crew experience, and gate locations were similar for both aircraft types, the aircraft model itself remains a plausible explanation for the difference in on-time rates.
quests.goldenRule: A valid conclusion is the natural destination of the premise chain; if any link breaks, the conclusion collapses.

candidatesDiagnosis.option: Crew experience differences are definitely responsible for the on-time rate difference.
candidatesDiagnosis.diagnosis: Directly conflicts with one or more observed facts in the passage.

candidatesDiagnosis.option: The newer aircraft were flown on entirely different routes than the older ones.
candidatesDiagnosis.diagnosis: Focuses on incidental topics not causally linked to the core premise chain.

candidatesDiagnosis.option: On-time departure rates showed no relationship to any aircraft characteristic.
candidatesDiagnosis.diagnosis: Leaps beyond the verified chain of evidence; introduces unstated assumptions.

candidatesDiagnosis.option: Since routes, crew experience, and gate locations were similar for both aircraft types, the aircraft model itself remains a plausible explanation for the difference in on-time rates.
candidatesDiagnosis.diagnosis: Necessarily follows from the established premises in the logic chain.

quests.explanation: Since the passage explicitly rules out route, crew experience, and gate differences as explanations by stating they were similar for both aircraft types, this leaves the aircraft model itself, perhaps through newer technology or fewer mechanical issues, as the more plausible remaining explanation.
